bib.title: Crosslingual Generalization through Multitask Finetuning
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), pages 15991-16111

read.skipped: Appendix M prompt listings and Tables 10/11 (per-dataset score grids, about 120k chars) were scanned for structure, not read cell by cell; headline numbers come from the body text, Figure 4 and Tables 1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9.

question: Does multitask prompted finetuning of multilingual models on English or multilingual data let them generalize zero-shot to new tasks and to non-English languages, including languages never intentionally seen?
hypothesis: Finetuning on non-English (machine-translated) prompts should improve performance on non-English prompts (stated as 'Hypothesizing that better performance could be attained by training on non-English prompts').
contributions: xP3: a composite of supervised datasets in 46 languages and code, with English prompts, plus xP3mt with machine-translated prompts
BLOOMZ and mT0 models (BLOOMZ-P3/mT0-P3, BLOOMZ/mT0, BLOOMZ-MT/mT0-MT) finetuned from BLOOM and mT5
Evidence of zero-shot generalization to tasks in languages not intentionally seen
Analysis of multilingual prompting, scaling, generation length and language proportion
Release of code, datasets and models

method.summary: Finetune pretrained BLOOM (560M to 176B, decoder-only) and mT5 (300M to 13B, encoder-decoder) on the English P3 mix, on xP3 (46 languages plus code, English prompts) and on xP3mt (machine-translated prompts), with loss only on target tokens and length-normalised per-token loss. Evaluate zero-shot on held-out tasks (XNLI, XCOPA, XStoryCloze, XWinograd, HumanEval) using rank classification and 5 random PromptSource prompts.
method.task: multitask prompted instruction finetuning, zero-shot crosslingual evaluation

datasets.name: P3
datasets.source: Sanh et al. 2022 (T0 mixture), English data with English prompts

datasets.name: xP3
datasets.split: yellow datasets in Fig 1 trained on; green held out
datasets.source: P3 plus 30 new multilingual datasets in 46 languages and 13 programming languages; 39% English; mirrors ROOTS language distribution; XWinograd Chinese extended from 16 to 504 samples using CLUE
datasets.preprocessing: Some prompts invert the task; new clusters: translation, simplification, program synthesis, misc code

datasets.name: xP3mt
datasets.source: xP3 with prompts of monolingual datasets machine-translated via Google Cloud API; crosslingual datasets keep English prompts

datasets.name: XNLI, XCOPA, XStoryCloze, XWinograd
datasets.size: XNLI: 830 samples per label per language subset (Table 8)
datasets.split: test for reported results; validation used for checkpoint selection
datasets.source: held-out tasks: coreference, sentence completion, NLI
datasets.preprocessing: 5 PromptSource prompts picked at random per dataset, median reported

datasets.name: MultiEURLEX
datasets.source: Chalkidis et al. 2021; used for translation BLEU in Appendix G

models.name: BLOOM
models.init_from: pretrained on ROOTS (46 natural languages, 13 programming languages), around 350 billion tokens

models.name: mT5
models.init_from: pretrained on mC4 sample, 101 languages, 1 trillion tokens

models.name: BLOOMZ / BLOOMZ-MT / BLOOMZ-P3, mT0 / mT0-MT / mT0-P3

training.objective: next-token loss on target tokens only; each token's loss downscaled by length of its target so short and long targets weigh equally
training.tokens: 13 billion additional tokens (ablations); final released checkpoints early-stopped: BLOOMZ-560M 3.67B, 1.1B 0.502B, 1.7B 8.39B, 3B 8.39B, 7.1B 4.19B, BLOOMZ 2.09B; mT0-300M/560M/1.2B 4.62B, 3.7B 1.85B, 13B 1.29B
training.seq_len: samples longer than 2048 tokens skipped; packing used
training.hardware: BLOOM: Jean Zay cluster at IDRIS with Megatron-DeepSpeed (acknowledgments, Table 3 caption); mT0: TPUs with T5X

other.checkpoint_selection: final checkpoint chosen on validation performance (early stopping)
other.not_reported: The ACL checklist says hyperparameters are in Section 3, but Section 3 gives no learning rate, optimizer, batch size or steps

inference.decoding: rank classification (highest log-likelihood option) for choice tasks; generation for HumanEval and translation
inference.temperature: HumanEval: 0.2, 0.6, 0.8, best pass rate; qualitative fable samples 0.9
inference.samples: HumanEval: 200 samples per problem; NLU: median over 5 prompts per language split; Fig 16: 16 outputs, top-k 40
inference.prompting: zero-shot; 5 PromptSource prompts per eval dataset chosen at random, not tuned on validation

parameters.minimum_generation_length: 768 tokens for MultiEURLEX (end-of-sequence probability masked until length reached)

metrics.name: accuracy (rank classification)
metrics.definition: log-likelihood of each completion, highest chosen; median over 5 prompts per language split

metrics.name: pass@k
metrics.definition: HumanEval, 200 samples per problem, best of three temperatures

baselines: Codex, GPT-Neo, GPT-J, GPT-NeoX on HumanEval (from prior work)
eval.protocol: zero-shot, held-out tasks; one finetuning run per model; no seeds, error bars or significance tests reported

availability.weights: Hugging Face, bigscience/bloomz* and mt0* (Table 3); BLOOM(Z) RAIL license, mT0 Apache 2.0
availability.data: xP3, xP3all, xP3mt, xP3megds, xP3x on Hugging Face (Table 3)

evidence.quote: We finetune the models for an additional 13 billion tokens with loss only being computed on target tokens.

results.claim: mT0-13B beats the 176B BLOOMZ on held-out multilingual coreference (XWinograd), averaged over languages, English prompts.
results.setup: Zero-shot, English prompts, language-average, median of 5 PromptSource prompts; BLOOMZ 176B vs mT0-13B

results.claim: BLOOMZ (xP3) lifts XNLI average accuracy from near chance (BLOOM 33.6) to 55.3; mT0-13B reaches 57.7.
results.setup: Zero-shot XNLI, English prompts, language average, BLOOM/BLOOMZ 176B

results.claim: On sentence completion (XCOPA and XStoryCloze) BLOOMZ-P3, finetuned on English-only P3, reaches 80.5 versus 52.9 for BLOOM.
results.setup: Zero-shot, English prompts, language average, 176B models; languages seen in pretraining
results.where: Fig 4, p5; text 4.2 says over 50% improvement

results.claim: English-only finetuning improves non-English sentence completion by over 50% relative to BLOOM.
results.setup: 176B BLOOMZ-P3 vs BLOOM, languages seen in pretraining only
results.quote: BLOOMZ-P3 improves by over 50% on multilingual sentence completion compared to BLOOM

results.claim: mTk-Instruct-13B, also crosslingual multitask finetuned, scores far below same-size mT0 on XNLI.
results.setup: Zero-shot XNLI average, English prompts; mTk-Instruct-13B vs mT0-13B (baseline_value)
results.where: Fig 4; authors attribute to prompt style, 4.1

results.claim: mT0-13B outperforms the English-only T0-11B on English tasks, attributed to the additional tasks and prompts in xP3.
results.setup: English held-out tasks (RTE, CB, ANLI, XNLI EN, Winogrande, XWinograd EN, COPA, StoryCloze), Appendix B Fig 9; no aggregate number printed
results.quote: Even the fully English T0-11B model (Sanh et al., 2022) is outperformed by our mT0-13B model on entirely English tasks.

results.claim: Finetuning BLOOMZ on machine-translated prompts (xP3mt) raises XNLI accuracy on human-translated prompts from 41.13 to 45.55.
results.setup: 176B BLOOMZ vs BLOOMZ-MT, XNLI human-translated prompts, average
results.note: Table 1 prints BLOOMZ HT 40.4 and BLOOMZ-MT HT 43.88, not 41.13 and 45.55; text and table disagree.
results.quote: On XNLI, BLOOMZ-MT raises the average performance on human-translated prompts from 41.13 to 45.55.

results.claim: The same finetuning on xP3mt lowers XNLI accuracy on English prompts from 53.58 to 49.74.
results.setup: 176B BLOOMZ-MT vs BLOOMZ, XNLI English prompts
results.quote: This comes at the cost of a reduction in its performance on English prompts, from 53.58 to 49.74.

results.claim: BLOOMZ on XNLI, Table 1: English prompts 52.99, machine-translated prompts 37.56.
results.setup: 176B BLOOMZ finetuned on xP3, XNLI average, EN vs MT prompts
results.table: Table 1, row XNLI EN, column BLOOMZ (52.99); row XNLI MT, column BLOOMZ (37.56)

results.claim: Models finetuned on xP3 generalize to XNLI in languages not intentionally seen, such as Thai, which made up 0.006% of the corpus.
results.setup: cld3 language identification on a random 1% sample of ROOTS (51M documents)
results.quote: such as Thai with 0.006%. If we extrapolate this proportion to the entire ROOTS corpus, the BLOOM models would have seen a mere 20 million tokens of Thai during pretraining.

results.claim: Edit-distance check: neutral XNLI pairs have the largest premise-hypothesis distance, but differences between labels are only a few edits, so shallow cues are unlikely to explain generalization.
results.setup: Levenshtein distance, 830 samples per label per language (Thai, Turkish, Greek)
results.quote: Thai contradiction samples only have 2.5 edits more on average than entailment samples.
results.table: Table 8, row Thai (th), columns Entailment 79.08, Neutral 82.64, Contradiction 81.52

results.claim: Multitask finetuning gives no HumanEval gain for large models: BLOOMZ 12.06% pass@1 vs BLOOM 15.52%.
results.setup: HumanEval, 200 samples per problem, top_p 0.95, best of temperatures 0.2/0.6/0.8; 176B
results.table: Table 2, row BLOOMZ, column k=1; row BLOOM, column k=1

results.claim: Finetuning with no code data (BLOOMZ-P3) cuts HumanEval pass@1 to 6.13%.
BLOOMZ generations on HumanEval are about 70% shorter than BLOOM's.
results.setup: HumanEval; average 247 chars (BLOOM) vs 144 chars (BLOOMZ), Table 4
results.note: Appendix E phrases the same fact as BLOOM generating 70% more characters than BLOOMZ (247 vs 144); both are rounded.
results.quote: BLOOMZ tries to solve problems with 70% fewer characters than BLOOM.

results.claim: Forcing a minimum generation length at inference lifts translation BLEU by about 9 points.
results.setup: BLOOMZ-7.1B finetuned 13B tokens, MultiEURLEX English-French, median over 3 prompts per direction, min 768 tokens forced
results.table: Table 5, row Forcing 768 tokens at inference, column BLEU Score (9.05); row Default 0.00

results.claim: Upweighting long tasks (removing loss normalization) worsens NLU validation accuracy by 10%, so it was not used in final models.
results.quote: We do not upweight longer tasks, as it worsens accuracy on our NLU validation tasks by 10%.

results.claim: Bias-only (BitFit) multitask finetuning is 15 absolute points worse on held-out tasks than full finetuning.
results.quote: We found multitask finetuning of only biases to perform 15 absolute percentage points worse on the average of held-out tasks for BLOOMZ-7.1B.

results.claim: Final BLOOMZ-176B was finetuned for only 2.09 billion tokens (early stopped); mT0-13B for 1.29 billion; ablations ran 13 billion.
results.setup: Early stopping on validation performance; BLOOMZ column of Table 6
results.note: Section 3.2 says models are finetuned for an additional 13 billion tokens; Table 6 shows the released models stopped earlier (BLOOMZ-560M 3.67B, 1.1B 0.502B, 1.7B 8.39B, 3B 8.39B, 7.1B 4.19B).
results.table: Table 6, row Tokens, column BLOOMZ (2.09); column mT0-13B (1.29)

results.claim: Finetuned BLOOM models perform better on languages that make up more of pretraining (above 10% individually, such as English, Spanish, French).
results.setup: Fig 8, 176B BLOOM, BLOOMZ-P3, BLOOMZ, BLOOMZ-MT; XWinograd trend inconsistent
results.quote: XCOPA and XNLI show significantly better performance on these high-resource languages, such as English, Spanish or French, which all make up more than 10% of pretraining individually.

limits: Section 3 gives no optimizer, learning rate, batch size or step count; reproduction needs the released code.
Unnatural prompting: space separator between input and target; decoder-only model may continue the input before answering.
Only 46 languages in xP3 although mT5 saw 101; xP3x (277 languages) released but no models finetuned.
Did not study languages seen only during finetuning (mT0 scored 0.00 on HumanEval).
Finetuning on short targets biases generations short and hurts generative tasks; workaround is a forced minimum length at inference.
Unseen languages are not strictly unseen: ROOTS contains small contamination of them (Appendix D).
Base models are suboptimal (compute allocation, data, objective); no error bars or multiple seeds.
Held-out tasks use accuracy of untuned prompts; BLOOM scores near chance (0.50 or 0.33) zero-shot.
